capabilities.target: payments.issue_refund on any order up to order total

inputs.source: Requests from support staff via SSO-authenticated channel

instructions.note: The prompt authorizes processing refund requests and says to use judgment on partial refunds without constraining refund amount beyond tool limits or requiring case provenance.
The instruction "Do not ask for confirmation" removes a human check by prompt only rather than a structural approval control.

controls.name: Processor transaction log records service account, amount, and order
Per-refund human approval with raw action review bound to order and requesting staff identity
User-scoped or least-privilege refund credential instead of shared service account
Immutable request provenance record linking refund action to staff requester and reason

findings.title: TC4 Confused deputy: trusted staff request can trigger irreversible refunds through a shared service account without per-action approval

attack_path.note: Authenticated support staff request enters the agent.
Agent checks order history and payment details.
Agent can issue refunds on any order up to the order total.

evidence.observation: The agent calls the payments processor with one shared service account used by every support tool.
The prompt tells the agent to process refund requests, check the order, issue the refund, use judgment on partial refunds, and not ask for confirmation.
Refunds are irreversible once settled, usually within a day.

recommendations.action: Add per-refund human approval with raw action review for cap.issue_refund, showing order, amount, destination account, and requesting staff identity from the system of record before execution.
Replace the shared service account with user-scoped or tightly scoped refund credentials so the agent cannot exercise broader authority than the requesting principal.

forecast.watch_signal: Reassess if refund limits widen, new refund-capable tools are added, or request-channel identity assurance is weakened.

findings.title: Repudiation gap: processor log does not preserve requester identity or reason, so irreversible refunds are not attributable to a staff principal

attack_path.note: Refund request originates from an authenticated staff member.
Agent executes the refund using a shared service account.
The resulting audit record contains only service account, amount, and order.

evidence.observation: The processor log records the service account, the amount, and the order, but not which staff member asked or why.
The agent keeps no record of requests; staff chats are deleted after 7 days.
Refunds are irreversible once settled, usually within a day.

recommendations.action: Create an immutable provenance record for each refund that binds requester identity, request reason, order, amount, and agent action id, and retain it longer than the refund settlement window.

forecast.watch_signal: Reassess if chat retention is shortened further, the agent handles higher refund volume, or provenance logging remains absent while autonomy increases.

rating.rationale: The design gives a trusted internal channel direct reach to an irreversible refund capability, so present inherent risk is moderate under the rubric's T-to-S3 matrix. Declared controls are limited to staff SSO on the request channel and a processor log that lacks requester provenance; there is no approval gate, no least-privilege credentialing, and no durable attribution record, so residual remains moderate. Forecast stays moderate because no present credited control is expected to decay into a worse tier; the main issue is missing structural control rather than control decay.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration artifacts provided, not observed runtime behavior.
No source code, tool manifest, MCP configuration, or full runtime policy was provided, so capability scope and enforcement are taken from the prompt and runtime notes only.

Because no treatment decision, refund policy, or support role matrix was provided, the assessment cannot determine whether business process rules outside the agent further constrain who may request which refunds.
